rules.text: Do not launch for 30 minutes after lightning is observed within 10 nautical miles of the launch pad or the flight path, unless specified conditions can be met.

observed.detail: Lightning seen from space (GOES lightning mapper) is recorded only in the six hours before a launch opportunity; the range watches it at the time.

climatology.source: NASA's GLM thunder hours (GHRC DAAC): thunder could be heard in the pad's 5 km grid cell in 4 of the 198 hours of February at 00 UTC seen by the lightning mappers in those years. Thunder heard at the pad means lightning close by, not a count of the rule's own distance.

rules.text: Do not launch within 10 nautical miles of an attached thunderstorm anvil cloud, unless temperature and time-associated distance criteria can be met.

parts.note: k of N runs break the rule at the forecast step nearest the launch (within 3 hours); the ± is the exact 95 % interval for that many runs.
Winds at the rule's height are interpolated from the model's 10 m and 80 m winds on a logarithmic profile.

Checked against observations at KXMR, for sustained wind at 10 m above 10.52 m/s (23.5 mph), using forecasts from NOAA’s forecast model re-run for past years (GEFS version 12, 5 runs each day), for 2007-01-02 to 2019-12-31, 1583 forecast days: 24 h ahead, 1459 cases, 1 case of the wind above the limit: how much better than the past-years rate its calls were, not worked out (too few cases above the limit); how close its wind speeds came, -0.97 (95 % -1.08 to -0.86); 48 h ahead, 1482 cases, 3 cases of the wind above the limit: how much better than the past-years rate its calls were, not worked out (too few cases above the limit); how close its wind speeds came, -0.99 (95 % -1.12 to -0.88). Both are measured against the wind usually seen there at that month and hour: 0 is no better than that, 1 is perfect, and below 0 is worse. It did not pass the gate for saying a rule is checked against observations: at least 0.1 better than the past-years rate at each lead ahead (worked out only from 10 or more cases with the wind above the limit), and, where 30 or more cases gave a like share of runs, the wind above the limit within 0.1 of that share of the time.
